identity.name: ASSO ALCOHOLS & BREW LTD
identity.industry: Alcohol & Beverage / Premium IMFL & Craft Spirits

summary.oneLiner: AABL shifted from licensing to contract manufacturing in IMFL, driving 32% YoY volume growth in proprietary brands despite flattish top line; the strategic focus on proprietary portfolio, new product launches (RTD, tequila, single malt), and acquisition of SDF Industries to control bottling is positioning it as a future-ready premium alco-bev player with 50% revenue target from own brands in 5 years.

one-line thesis: AABL shifted from licensing to contract manufacturing in IMFL, driving 32% YoY volume growth in proprietary brands despite flattish top line; the strategic focus on proprietary portfolio, new product launches (RTD, tequila, single malt), and acquisition of SDF Industries to control bottling is positioning it as a future-ready premium alco-bev player with 50% revenue target from own brands in 5 years.
financial scorecard: revenue: flat YoY (INR1,000cr FY26) due to Inbrew transition; EBITDA/margin: +13% YoY to INR40cr (Q4), 17% margin (up 200 bps); PAT: +5% YoY to INR24cr (Q4), normalized PAT higher due to one-off Inbrew restructuring costs; order book: not disclosed; net debt: net debt-free
guidance: revenue growth: 10%+ YoY FY27; margin: 15% EBITDA margin target FY27; order inflow: none specified; capex/commissioning: INR10cr for SDF modernization, INR70cr total capex planned FY27 (includes SDF and malt facility ramp-up)
segment / subsidiary detail: Proprietary IMFL: 37% YoY volume growth to 6.6L cases, 38% revenue growth to INR50cr, 22% EBITDA margin (all-time high); IMFL (contract): revenue +7% YoY to INR62cr, 20% margin; Ethanol: volume -35% YoY to 4M liters, revenue INR24cr, 10% margin; Merchant ENA: volume +129% YoY to 6.9M liters, revenue +128% to INR47cr, 14% margin
growth verticals / optionality: RTD (Kultur) soft-launched in MP, label approvals pending in 14 states; tequila launch delayed to H1 FY27 due to shipping; single malt to launch H2 FY28 (FY29 full year); expansion into Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka; target 50% revenue from proprietary IMFL in 3-5 years
margins & cost dynamics: IMFL proprietary margin expected to normalize to 15-17% as premium marketing spends rise; packaging cost inflation (PET, paper, aluminum) mitigated via value engineering (e.g., removing mono cartons); ethanol margin at 7-10% EBITDA, not core but supports scale
capex / expansion: INR70cr total planned for FY27: INR30cr for SDF acquisition, INR10cr for SDF automation/modernization, remaining for malt facility scaling and bottling line upgrades
capital allocation: Prioritizing proprietary IMFL growth, backward integration (malt plant, bottling via SDF), and premium product launches; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; net debt-free position enables organic investment
risks & watch-items: Ethanol volume dependency on government blending policy (20%→25%); regulatory delays in RTD/tequila approvals; premium brand adoption lag in new states; packaging cost volatility; competition from Bacardi Breezer in RTD and established players in single malt
management quality / tone: Confident, strategic, long-term oriented; clear focus on proprietary brands, operational control, and premiumization; transparent about challenges (ethanol, tequila delays); proactive on backward integration
non-obvious takeaways: SDF acquisition is not just about capacity—it’s a strategic geographic play (central Kerala location, proximity to airports) to solve bottling fragmentation and enable faster SKU rollout; single malt maturation already underway with blending exceeding expectations; ENA surplus is being cannibalized for own IMFL use, reducing external malt purchases

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Present across the entire liquor value chain - IMFL Proprietary, IMFL Licensed, IMIL, Merchant ENA and Ethanol - with by-products (cattle feed) monetised alongside, described as the largest integrated manufacturing facility at a single location.
- Two decades of partnership with Diageo and status as one of only four exclusive Diageo contract manufacturing partners; also contract manufactures for Inbrew, giving a captive B2B volume base.
- Dominant IMFL footprint in Madhya Pradesh and Keralam, where it is a top-3 private player with ~1.5% market share (FY26) and was the fastest to reach 1 million cases in under four years after 2018 entry.
- Centrally located in the heart of India, giving equidistant access to raw-material mandis and distribution hubs across the country; claims to be the first company in the world to make White Brandy (Lemount).
- Present in 14 states/UTs including MP, Chhattisgarh, Keralam, Delhi, West Bengal, UP, Maharashtra, Goa, Jharkhand, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Manipur and Odisha.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] SDF Industries acquired via an IBC resolution plan approved by NCLT Kochi on 16 April 2026 for Rs 30.85 Cr; it becomes a wholly owned subsidiary and brings Kerala bottling in-house.
- [Business model change] The Inbrew arrangement shifted from licensing to contract manufacturing, structurally reducing reported IMFL licensed volumes without an equivalent economic loss.
- [Segment headwind] Ethanol faces industry oversupply that management expects to persist for the rest of the financial year, and the segment reported an operating loss in Q1FY27.
- [Industry] Indian alco-bev market sized at INR 3,255 Bn in 2024 heading to INR 5,763 Bn by 2030P; premium & luxury alco-bev at INR 28,751 Cr in 2024 to INR 50,000 Cr by 2029E, with whisky over 70% of IMFL.
- [Leadership] Promoter-led board (Prasann Kumar Kedia MD, Anshuman Kedia WTD & CEO) supplemented by senior hires from Pernod Ricard India and United Spirits in sales and marketing.
